title: The Concept of Phenomenal Consciousness
text:
Phenomenal consciousness refers to the subjective, qualitative feel of experience—what it is like to see red or feel pain. This aspect of awareness distinguishes conscious perception from mere information processing, suggesting that raw data must undergo a transformation into meaningful qualia.

Philosophical debates surrounding this concept often center on the 'hard problem' of consciousness: explaining how physical brain processes give rise to subjective experience. Materialist theories generally seek to reduce these qualia to neuronal activity or complex computation, while dualistic views posit that mind and matter are fundamentally different substances.
